children: Australia spent heavily on imported technology, electric vehicles and energy in 2Q as it responded to the Middle East crisis and the race to facilitate artificial intelligence, says Cherelle Murphy, chief economist at EY. But the composition of growth was less encouraging than the headline suggests. Much of the additional private sector spending leaked into imports, productivity went backwards over the year, and price pressures persisted. The data will do little to ease the Reserve Bank of Australia's concerns about the inflation outlook, she says. (james.glynn@wsj.com; X @JamesGlynnWSJ)
